head: 73b59f16cebafa3f879255a0a11865691d6411d8
claim: On a real Mac, an opted-in desktop session delivers the person's clicks and key presses as session.input.observed events (with button, key, modifiers) in source pixels.

verdicts.seen: I read all 22 session.input.observed entries: 6 pointer events (buttons 1, 3, 2 with down/up at source x 1400 to 2200, y 20) and 16 key events (Shift, h, i, Control, c, F13, Enter, ArrowLeft, down/up), each carrying modifiers. Coordinates exceed the 1710-wide encoded frame, so they are source pixels. inputObservation shows mechanism cgeventtap with observing true, which is macOS-specific. The key entries use name/character rather than a literal 'key' field, a minor naming difference. The outcome names one result, so no parts.

The menu bar reads "Simulator" with a macOS clock, so this is a Mac screen. The visible text reads "button 1 down at 1400,20" and "observed on the engine clock, source pixels = 2x frame pixels." That matches the outcome's button and source-pixel input reporting. The exact event name session.input.observed is not visible, so this is not fully confirmed.
